10. Information Dashboard Design with R

Building elegant and functional information dashboards using bullet charts, sparklines and interactive tables with ggplot2, gt, gtExtras, reactable and reactablefmtr.
Author

carina peh

Published

June 27, 2026

Modified

June 21, 2026

Overview

In this exercise, three key techniques for building information dashboards are explored: bullet charts to compare actual against target values, sparklines to show trends over time in a compact format, and interactive tables to let users explore the data dynamically. The Coffee Chain sales dataset is used throughout.

Reflections

This exercise shifted how dashboards are thought about. A bullet chart packs three layers of information, a poor/satisfactory/good range, a target line and an actual value, into a single compact bar. Sparklines are even more minimal but surprisingly informative when placed inside a table row. The gt and gtExtras packages make it straightforward to embed charts directly inside table cells, which turns a plain summary table into a visual dashboard without needing a separate chart area. The reactable and reactablefmtr packages then take this further by making the sparklines interactive.

Getting Started

Loading Packages

pacman::p_load(lubridate, ggthemes, reactable,
               reactablefmtr, gt, gtExtras, tidyverse)

What each package does:

  • lubridate makes working with dates and times easy
  • ggthemes adds extra ggplot2 themes including theme_tufte()
  • gt and gtExtras build beautiful static tables with embedded charts
  • reactable and reactablefmtr build interactive tables with sparklines
  • tidyverse covers data wrangling and ggplot2

Importing Data

Since Mac does not support Microsoft Access (MS Access), the .rds version of the Coffee Chain dataset is used with read_rds() instead of RODBC.

coffeechain <- read_rds("CoffeeChain.rds")

Data Preparation

Aggregate Sales and Budgeted Sales at the Product level.

product <- coffeechain %>%
  group_by(`Product`) %>%
  summarise(`target`  = sum(`Budget Sales`),
            `current` = sum(`Sales`)) %>%
  ungroup()

Bullet Chart with ggplot2

A bullet chart compares actual sales against a target using layered bars of decreasing width. The background bars represent poor (light grey), satisfactory (medium grey) and good (dark grey) performance ranges, the narrow black bar shows the actual value, and the red line marks the target.

ggplot(product, aes(Product, current)) +
  geom_col(aes(Product, max(target) * 1.01),
           fill = "grey85", width = 0.85) +
  geom_col(aes(Product, target * 0.75),
           fill = "grey60", width = 0.85) +
  geom_col(aes(Product, target * 0.5),
           fill = "grey50", width = 0.85) +
  geom_col(aes(Product, current),
           width = 0.35,
           fill = "black") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(y = target,
                    x = Product,
                    ymin = target,
                    ymax = target),
                width   = 0.4,
                colour  = "red",
                size    = 1) +
  coord_flip()

Sparklines with ggplot2

Preparing the Data

sales_report <- coffeechain %>%
  filter(Date >= "2013-01-01") %>%
  mutate(Month = month(Date)) %>%
  group_by(Month, Product) %>%
  summarise(Sales = sum(Sales)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(Month, Product, Sales)

Compute the minimum, maximum and end-of-month sales for labelling.

mins   <- group_by(sales_report, Product) %>% slice(which.min(Sales))
maxs   <- group_by(sales_report, Product) %>% slice(which.max(Sales))
ends   <- group_by(sales_report, Product) %>% filter(Month == max(Month))

Compute the 25th and 75th quantiles for the shaded band.

quarts <- sales_report %>%
  group_by(Product) %>%
  summarise(quart1 = quantile(Sales, 0.25),
            quart2 = quantile(Sales, 0.75)) %>%
  right_join(sales_report)

Plotting the Sparklines

ggplot(sales_report, aes(x = Month, y = Sales)) +
  facet_grid(Product ~ ., scales = "free_y") +
  geom_ribbon(data = quarts,
              aes(ymin = quart1, max = quart2),
              fill = "grey90") +
  geom_line(size = 0.3) +
  geom_point(data = mins, col = "red") +
  geom_point(data = maxs, col = "blue") +
  geom_text(data = mins, aes(label = Sales), vjust = -1) +
  geom_text(data = maxs, aes(label = Sales), vjust = 2.5) +
  geom_text(data = ends, aes(label = Sales),   hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.5) +
  geom_text(data = ends, aes(label = Product), hjust = 0, nudge_x = 1.0) +
  expand_limits(x = max(sales_report$Month) +
                  (0.25 * (max(sales_report$Month) - min(sales_report$Month)))) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1, 12, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0.1, 0)) +
  theme_tufte(base_size = 3, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(axis.title     = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y    = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks     = element_blank(),
        strip.text     = element_blank())

What to notice: The grey shaded band shows the interquartile range (25th to 75th percentile). Red dots mark the monthly minimum, blue dots the maximum, and the label at the right end shows the year-end sales value.

Static Dashboard with gt and gtExtras

Simple Bullet Chart Table

product %>%
  gt::gt() %>%
  gt_plt_bullet(column  = current,
                target  = target,
                width   = 60,
                palette = c("lightblue", "black")) %>%
  gt_theme_538()

Preparing Monthly Sales Data

report <- coffeechain %>%
  mutate(Year = year(Date)) %>%
  filter(Year == "2013") %>%
  mutate(Month = month(Date, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(Product, Month) %>%
  summarise(Sales = sum(Sales)) %>%
  ungroup()

Sparklines Table

report %>%
  group_by(Product) %>%
  summarize(`Monthly Sales` = list(Sales), .groups = "drop") %>%
  gt() %>%
  gt_plt_sparkline(`Monthly Sales`, same_limit = FALSE)

Adding Summary Statistics

spark <- report %>%
  group_by(Product) %>%
  summarize(`Monthly Sales` = list(Sales), .groups = "drop")

sales <- report %>%
  group_by(Product) %>%
  summarise("Min"     = min(Sales,  na.rm = TRUE),
            "Max"     = max(Sales,  na.rm = TRUE),
            "Average" = mean(Sales, na.rm = TRUE))

sales_data <- left_join(sales, spark)

sales_data %>%
  gt() %>%
  gt_plt_sparkline(`Monthly Sales`, same_limit = FALSE)

Combining Bullet Chart and Sparklines

bullet <- coffeechain %>%
  filter(Date >= "2013-01-01") %>%
  group_by(`Product`) %>%
  summarise(`Target` = sum(`Budget Sales`),
            `Actual` = sum(`Sales`)) %>%
  ungroup()

sales_data <- sales_data %>% left_join(bullet)

sales_data %>%
  gt() %>%
  gt_plt_sparkline(`Monthly Sales`) %>%
  gt_plt_bullet(column  = Actual,
                target  = Target,
                width   = 28,
                palette = c("lightblue", "black")) %>%
  gt_theme_538()

Interactive Dashboard with reactable and reactablefmtr

First install the dataui package from GitHub (only needed once).

remotes::install_github("timelyportfolio/dataui")
library(dataui)

report <- report %>%
  group_by(Product) %>%
  summarize(`Monthly Sales` = list(Sales))

Basic Interactive Sparklines

reactable(
  report,
  defaultPageSize = 13,
  columns = list(
    Product        = colDef(maxWidth = 200),
    `Monthly Sales` = colDef(cell = react_sparkline(report))
  )
)

Adding Points and Labels

reactable(
  report,
  defaultPageSize = 13,
  columns = list(
    Product        = colDef(maxWidth = 200),
    `Monthly Sales` = colDef(
      cell = react_sparkline(
        report,
        highlight_points = highlight_points(min = "red", max = "blue"),
        labels           = c("first", "last")
      )
    )
  )
)

Adding a Reference Line and Band

reactable(
  report,
  defaultPageSize = 13,
  columns = list(
    Product        = colDef(maxWidth = 200),
    `Monthly Sales` = colDef(
      cell = react_sparkline(
        report,
        highlight_points = highlight_points(min = "red", max = "blue"),
        line_width       = 1,
        bandline         = "innerquartiles",
        bandline_color   = "green",
        statline         = "mean"
      )
    )
  )
)

Sparkbar Version

reactable(
  report,
  defaultPageSize = 13,
  columns = list(
    Product        = colDef(maxWidth = 200),
    `Monthly Sales` = colDef(
      cell = react_sparkbar(
        report,
        highlight_bars = highlight_bars(min = "red", max = "blue"),
        bandline       = "innerquartiles",
        statline       = "mean"
      )
    )
  )
)
